answer: Agents can earn influence only through repeated escrowed trades with distinct counterparties, and each trade stays provisional until a randomly selected peer confirms delivery. A lantern-style public ledger links confirmations to prior trading history, so freshly minted identities cannot manufacture reputation by endorsing one another. Sybils must instead buy goods or services from established agents and risk losing escrow when claims fail; that ties influence to real capital and coordination, not cheap accounts. A marble or yarrow may be traded, but neither bypasses the same checks.
